title: Eliminate the common plate: pairwise differential plateless capacitors
idea: Remove the shared top-plate electrode and its conformal TiN/poly fill; neighbouring pillar storage nodes face each other through the high-k film so each pair forms one capacitor written with complementary charge (+Q/-Q) and read differentially on a folded bitline pair.
why: Capacitor charge wall: differential read roughly doubles signal per unit Cs, so ~5 fF pillars behave like ~9-10 fF single-ended; deletes the plate deposition/etch module.

title: Eliminate the landing pad: oxide capacitor grown self-aligned on channel
idea: Delete the storage-node contact and landing-pad litho layer; grow a conductive perovskite oxide (e.g. SrRuO3 or LaNiO3) by selective-area epitaxy only on the exposed top of each vertical channel, so the capacitor bottom electrode self-registers to the transistor with zero overlay margin.
why: Litho-bound scaling: removes one critical (often EUV) layer and its overlay budget, enabling true 4F2 without pad-to-pillar misalignment; ~10-15% cost/bit.

title: Eliminate the 3D staircase: contact tiers at the etched die sidewall
idea: Remove the NAND-style staircase entirely; terminate every tier at a deep-etched trench wall at the mat edge where all tiers are exposed edge-on, then a laser-written or tilted-deposition redistribution layer fans each tier out to the top surface.
why: No manufacturable 3D DRAM: the staircase costs area and N trim/etch cycles; edge contacting makes tier count nearly free in area, helping reach the 26+ tier break-even.

title: Eliminate the access transistor: 1-selector-1-capacitor cross-point decks
idea: Replace the transistor with a two-terminal threshold switch (Mott NbO2 or ovonic chalcogenide) in series with a planar MIM capacitor at every wordline/bitline crossing, stacked in 4-8 decks like cross-point memory; the selector snaps on above Vth to charge/read and blocks below it.
why: Density and capital: 4F2/deck with no epitaxial transistor per tier; trade-off is selector leakage, so targeted as a short-retention (ms) last-level working tier with fast refresh.

title: Eliminate the consumable wafer: foil arrays stacked like paper
idea: Build thin-film DRAM arrays on a reusable sapphire carrier, release each 2-5 um array foil by laser lift-off, and laminate dozens of foils into a stack with printed vertical vias; the carrier returns to the line hundreds of times.
why: Scarce-resource intensity: cuts Czochralski wafer (and Spruce Pine quartz crucible) consumption per bit by >10x and multiplies bits per footprint.

title: Eliminate TSV keep-out: vertical bus runs through scribe lines
idea: Stack whole memory wafers without singulating between dies in a column; place all vertical power and signal vias in the scribe streets that are otherwise wasted, so the active die area has zero TSV keep-out, and dice the finished stack once.
why: HBM TSV tax: removes TSV and keep-out area from the die (a large part of HBM's ~3x area/bit penalty) and avoids per-die thinning yield loss.

title: Eliminate the row decoder: token-ring sequential wordlines for weights
idea: For AI weight memory that is read in fixed order, replace random row decoders with a shift-register token chain along the mat edge that activates wordline n+1 after n; random access falls back to a small seek-and-stream jump table per bank.
why: Periphery ~49% of die: row decode/predecode area and energy drop by most of their share, giving ~10-15% die area and lower activation energy for streaming workloads.

title: Eliminate periphery from the memory wafer: subarray-granular hybrid bonding
idea: The memory wafer carries only cell arrays with 16:1 bitline muxes at each subarray edge; sense amps, decoders and I/O sit on a separately made logic wafer joined by ~400 nm pitch hybrid bonds at subarray granularity.
why: Periphery ~49%: array efficiency rises toward ~85-90%, and periphery moves to a cheaper or better-suited logic node; ~1.6x bits per memory wafer.

title: Eliminate tungsten wordlines: in-situ doped SiGe wordline tiers
idea: In a Si/SiGe superlattice 3D DRAM, keep the wordline tiers as heavily boron-doped epitaxial SiGe grown in the same epi run, with no replacement-gate metal fill, and use short segmented wordlines with local drivers to tolerate the higher resistance.
why: Scarce resource (China ~80% of tungsten) and process steps: removes the W replacement-gate module and its voids in deep lateral cavities.

title: Eliminate the high-AR capacitor etch: anodic alumina pore templates
idea: Skip plasma-etching capacitor holes; deposit thick aluminium over the transistor array, pre-dent it at each storage node, and anodize so self-ordered pores with aspect ratios above 500:1 grow straight down onto each node; line them with high-k and electrode.
why: Capacitor charge wall: the AR 115:1 needed for more charge comes from electrochemistry instead of a hard mask and etch, giving a ~2x Cs headroom with no hard mask.

title: Eliminate pitch-defining lithography: rotated superlattice slices
idea: Grow a 1000-period Si/SiGe or Si/oxide multilayer whose film thicknesses set the 10-12 nm line pitch, slice it perpendicular to the layers, and bond the slab flat so the layers become parallel bitlines/channels; litho is needed only for coarse cuts.
why: Litho and capital: replaces 5-7 EUV layers with epitaxy thickness control (Angstrom precision), attacking the ~55% depreciation share of wafer cost.

title: Eliminate planar sense-amp stripes: tier-flipped checkerboard mats
idea: In a two-or-more-tier stack, place the sense-amp strip of tier N directly above the cell mat of tier N+1 and vice versa in a checkerboard, so no footprint is spent on SA stripes and bitlines stay short.
why: Periphery ~49%: SA stripes (~15-20% of planar die) vanish from the footprint, and short bitlines raise the Cs/Cb ratio.

title: Eliminate the flat wafer surface: arrays built on trench sidewalls
idea: Etch 50-100 um-deep parallel trenches across the wafer and build DRAM cells on both vertical walls using tilted-implant and self-aligned spacer patterning, folding several square centimetres of array area into each square centimetre of footprint.
why: Density per footprint and per wafer: each wafer behaves like several wafers of area, cutting crystal-silicon and depreciation per bit if sidewall uniformity holds.

title: Eliminate the wafer fab entirely: thermally drawn fiber DRAM
idea: Assemble a macroscopic preform of semiconductor, glass and metal stripes encoding capacitor-transistor cross-sections, thermally draw it into kilometres of fiber with thousands of parallel nanoscale cells, then cut, align and tile fiber segments into planks addressed at their ends.
why: Capital intensity: replaces lithography with fiber-draw towers costing millions instead of billions; density and access speed are open questions.

title: Eliminate the separate memory die: DRAM on the logic backside
idea: Use the silicon freed by backside power delivery under a logic die to build a trench-capacitor DRAM array, connected to the frontside cache controllers by nano-TSVs at ~1 um pitch.
why: Data movement: memory sits 10 um under the cores, giving <0.5 pJ/bit access and removing a separate die, package and interposer for the first few GB.

title: Eliminate the big monolithic die: fluidically self-assembled mat-lets
idea: Fabricate 0.5-1 mm2 DRAM mat-lets (array plus local SA), test and bin them, then pour them onto a logic wafer where shape-matched recesses and capillary forces seat them before a batch bond.
why: Yield and capital: known-good small tiles avoid large-die yield loss, and mat-lets can come from many small older fabs, including U.S. lines.

title: Eliminate on-die charge pumps: VPP delivered from package PMIC
idea: Remove VPP, VBB and VBLH charge pumps and regulators from every DRAM die; supply them from one high-efficiency package-level PMIC through dedicated backside power vias shared across the stack.
why: Periphery and energy: pumps are a meaningful slice of periphery area and run at 30-50% efficiency; external DC-DC at ~85% cuts wordline-supply energy ~2x.

title: Eliminate on-die redundancy: system-level page retirement replaces spares
idea: Drop spare rows, columns and laser-fuse boxes; ship each die with a signed bad-region map that the memory controller and OS use to retire 4 KB pages, accepting a few tenths of a percent of lost capacity.
why: Cost per bit: recovers ~3-6% die area and removes laser repair and its test step from the back end.

title: Eliminate open-bitline dummy edge mats: self-referenced double sampling
idea: Replace reference-from-neighbour-mat sensing with a sense amp that samples its own bitline before and after charge sharing on a small on-SA capacitor, so the half-used dummy mats at array edges disappear.
why: Periphery/area: edge dummy mats waste ~3-5% of array area in open-bitline 6F2/4F2 designs; also gives better offset cancellation.

title: Eliminate electrical wordlines: optically gated photo-TFT access
idea: Replace metal wordlines and their 3 V drivers with a row-scanning micro-LED or waveguide grating that illuminates one row of photoconductive oxide-semiconductor access switches; dark switches have very low leakage, while lit ones conduct.
why: Voltage floor: the ~3 V wordline swing and its CV2 energy disappear, and row hammer from wordline coupling vanishes; switching speed is the open risk.

title: Eliminate the page: AND-gated two-transistor pillar cells
idea: In a vertical-bitline 3D array, each cell has two series access gates, a tier wordline and a pillar-select gate, so a cell connects only when both are high; one activation opens a single 64-tier pillar instead of an 8 Kb row.
why: 128x overfetch: activation energy per useful bit falls ~10-50x and row hammer shrinks because no full row is opened; the stack absorbs the second transistor's area.

title: Eliminate identical tiers: hot short-bitline tiers over dense tiers
idea: Build the top 4 tiers of a 3D stack with short bitlines and fast, frequently refreshed cells and the lower tiers with long bitlines and dense cells; an on-die migration engine moves hot rows upward over vertical bitline bridges.
why: Latency vs density: near-SRAM-class latency for the hot set and maximum density for the bulk in one stack, with ~20% lower average access energy.

title: Eliminate binary storage: three-level cells paired across adjacent tiers
idea: Store three charge levels per cell and pair cells vertically across two tiers so 9 states encode 3 bits in 2 cells; a shared vertical reference ladder in each pillar tracks temperature and leakage drift.
why: Density/cost per bit: +50% bits per cell pair with no extra lithography; needs ~2x sense margin, which short vertical bitlines provide.

title: Eliminate cells: vertical charge-coupled shift-register strings
idea: Delete the per-bit capacitor, transistor and staircase: each vertical hole through 128 tiers is a CCD whose tier gates are tied to only 3 clock phases, so charge packets shift up to a single sense node at the top (128 ns worst-case serial access, pipelined bursts).
why: Water: one hole etch plus one channel deposition serves 128 bits with no capacitor module or tier contacts, so wet cleans and CMP per bit drop by >10x; also removes capacitor charge-wall limits.

title: Eliminate the capacitor: volatile charge-trap strings with ultrathin tunnel oxide
idea: Build a vertical NAND-style string, but with a ~1.5 nm tunnel oxide so electrons enter and leave a nitride trap layer by direct tunnelling in tens of ns (retention of seconds, refreshed like DRAM), avoiding Fowler-Nordheim wear-out.
why: Water: reuses the 3D NAND flow, where one deep-hole litho and clean sequence covers 100+ tiers; wet steps per bit fall >10x versus 1T1C DRAM. Endurance at 1e15 cycles is the key risk.

title: Eliminate water rinses: supercritical CO2 cleaning of capacitor holes
idea: Replace post-etch wet cleans and IPA drying of high-AR capacitor holes with supercritical CO2 plus co-solvent cleaning and drying in one chamber, so no liquid-vapour meniscus ever forms inside the structures.
why: Water: removes the UPW rinses of the capacitor module, the most rinse-heavy part of the cell. Removing capillary collapse also unlocks the AR ~115:1 needed to break the charge wall.

title: Eliminate the oxide mold and HF dip-out: ashable carbon molds
idea: Form capacitor holes in an amorphous-carbon mold instead of oxide, deposit the electrode, then remove the mold with dry O2/H2 plasma ash, eliminating the HF wet dip-out and the rinse/dry steps where cylinders collapse.
why: Water: the dip-out and its rinses go away along with the oxide-mold CMP; combined with dry cleans, the capacitor module's water drops ~10x.

title: Eliminate the capacitor hole: bottom-up nanowire capacitor electrodes
idea: Instead of etching a mold, grow a conductive nanowire (doped Si or silicide, using a CMOS-safe Al or Sn catalyst) vapour-liquid-solid straight up from each storage node to AR 200:1, then wrap it in ALD high-k and plate.
why: Water and charge wall: no mold deposition, hole etch, polymer clean or dip-out, so most capacitor wet steps vanish; free-standing high-AR wires give ~2x Cs.

title: Eliminate sacrificial SiGe: Si/CaF2 epitaxial insulator superlattice
idea: Grow 3D DRAM tiers as an epitaxial superlattice of silicon and lattice-matched CaF2 (~0.6% mismatch), so the inter-tier insulator is grown in its final form and no sacrificial layer needs wet lateral removal and refill.
why: Water: removes the wet lateral SiGe recess, its rinses, and the refill/etch-back cycles of 3D DRAM tier formation; helps reach 26+ tiers with ~10x fewer wet steps per bit.

title: Eliminate etch-fill-polish cycles: flat-by-construction conversion patterning
idea: Define isolation and channels by locally converting silicon rather than removing it: patterned oxygen or nitrogen implant plus anneal (SIMOX-like) turns selected regions into insulator, so the surface stays planar and no gap-fill or CMP is needed.
why: Water: STI etch, fill, CMP and their cleans are among the heaviest UPW users per layer; a planar conversion flow removes them for the array, cutting array-module water ~10x.

title: Eliminate air breaks: never-break-vacuum linear cluster for tiers
idea: Deposit all channel, dielectric and electrode films for 32+ tiers in one linear vacuum cluster with in-situ remote-plasma hydrogen cleaning between steps, so there is never a native oxide and never a wet pre-clean.
why: Water: pre-deposition wet cleans are a large share of a fab's UPW; doing a whole tier stack in vacuum replaces dozens of rinses with one, per stack.

title: Eliminate photoresist: area-selective deposition self-aligned to lower tiers
idea: Use vapour-delivered inhibitor molecules that adsorb only on dielectric (or only on metal) so the next film grows only where the underlying tier's pattern allows, eliminating resist coat, aqueous TMAH develop and wet strip for self-aligned layers.
why: Water: each resist cycle carries develop, rinse and strip water; making contacts, caps and landing layers self-aligned removes most of them and also removes overlay error.

title: Eliminate immersion water and develop: nanoimprint for periodic layers
idea: Pattern the highly periodic array layers (active, wordline, bitline, capacitor holes) by UV nanoimprint with a master template; there is no immersion water film and no aqueous develop, and only the irregular periphery uses optical litho.
why: Water and capital: removes immersion UPW and developer rinses on array layers and avoids EUV for perfectly periodic patterns; ~5-10x lower litho water combined with dry cleans.

title: Eliminate copper damascene: subtractive molybdenum array wiring
idea: Pattern bitlines and local interconnect by dry etching a blanket molybdenum film (with self-aligned dry-etched vias) instead of copper electroplating plus CMP, removing plating baths, slurry and post-CMP brush cleans.
why: Water: metal ECD and CMP are among the most water-intensive steps; subtractive Mo is fully dry and also avoids copper diffusion barriers at narrow pitch.

title: Eliminate interlayer dielectric fill: vacuum-gap array wiring
idea: Leave the space between bitlines, wordlines and tiers as sealed vacuum cavities (pinch-off cap deposition) instead of gap-fill oxide followed by CMP, with nitride posts holding the structure.
why: Water and charge wall: no gap-fill CMP or its cleans, and bitline capacitance falls ~2x, so a ~2x smaller Cs gives the same signal and relaxes capacitor AR.

title: Eliminate the 12-die HBM stack: one monolithic 3D-tiered die
idea: Replace 12 thinned DRAM dies bonded with TSVs by one die with 48-96 monolithic array tiers over periphery, so there is a single grind, no TSV reveal CMP and no 11 repeated bond-surface preparations.
why: Water and HBM tax: backgrinding, TSV reveal CMP, bond prep cleans and dicing are repeated per die today; one die removes >90% of them and the TSV area tax.

title: Eliminate TSVs: shingled stacks with laser-written edge interconnect
idea: Stack dies offset like roof shingles so each die's pad row is exposed, then write vertical interconnect down the stepped edge with laser direct-write or aerosol-jet silver, with no TSV etch, liner, copper plating or reveal.
why: Water and TSV tax: the TSV module (etch, wet clean, ECD, reveal CMP) is the most water-heavy part of HBM; removing it gives ~10x lower stacking water and recovers the keep-out area.

title: Eliminate CMP before bonding: in-vacuum atomic diffusion bonding
idea: Stack tiers by sputtering a few nm of Ti or Au-free metal onto both surfaces in the same vacuum and pressing them together at room temperature (atomic diffusion bonding), with no CMP to 0.5 nm roughness and no wet surface activation.
why: Water: hybrid bonding's CMP plus megasonic clean is repeated per bonded tier; vacuum bonding is dry, cutting bonding water ~10x and enabling cheaper multi-tier stacks.

title: Eliminate wafer slicing and polishing: dry spalled kerfless donor films
idea: Peel 20-50 um silicon films from an ingot face by controlled spalling with a sputtered stressor layer instead of wire-sawing, lapping and polishing wafers, and use the films as thin tier donors for stacked arrays.
why: Water and scarce resource: wafering's slurry, saw coolant and polish rinses vanish, and kerf loss goes to zero, so ingots (and quartz crucibles) per bit drop ~2x and wafering water >10x.

title: Eliminate implant masks: junctionless in-situ doped access channels
idea: Grow channels in-situ doped during epitaxy or deposition and use junctionless accumulation-mode access transistors, removing source/drain and well implant masks with their resist strips and post-implant wet cleans.
why: Water: each implant layer costs resist develop, ash plus wet strip and rinse; removing 6-10 implant layers in the array cuts a major water block and also avoids junction leakage tails.

title: Eliminate the distinct periphery process: array-transistor-only periphery
idea: Build sense amps, decoders and drivers from the same vertical channel devices as the array, in a single homogeneous device process, accepting larger periphery circuits that are tucked under the array.
why: Water: the planar periphery CMOS flow (many wells, implants, gate stacks, salicide cleans) is ~40% of mask and wet steps; removing it and stacking tiers gives ~10x less water per bit.

title: Eliminate wafers and wet benches: roll-to-roll vacuum web tiers
idea: Deposit oxide-semiconductor capacitor-transistor tiers on a moving stainless or polyimide web inside a vacuum roll coater, patterning with in-line laser ablation and shadow-roll masks, then laminate cut sheets into stacks.
why: Water and capital: vacuum web coating uses almost no process water and costs tens of millions per line; it suits slower, higher-capacity working-memory tiers.

title: Eliminate TSVs: through-silicon optical links at 1310 nm
idea: Silicon is transparent at 1310 nm, so stacked thinned dies talk vertically through the bulk with micro-LED or VCSEL emitters and Ge photodiodes aligned in columns, with no drilled or plated vias.
why: Water and HBM tax: no TSV etch, wet clean, ECD or reveal CMP, and no keep-out zones; each optical column can carry tens of Gb/s.

title: Eliminate oxide CMP: vacuum glass reflow planarization
idea: Return to pre-CMP practice: cap each tier with a low-melting borophosphosilicate glass and reflow it under vacuum so surface tension planarizes it, with a dry etch-back to target thickness.
why: Water: dielectric CMP and post-CMP cleans recur on every tier of a 3D stack; reflow removes slurry and brush-clean water, roughly 10x per planarization step.

title: Eliminate the zero-defect assumption: defect-tolerant arrays allow fewer rinses
idea: Design mats with fine-grained remapping and per-mat ECC so random particle and metal defects cost capacity rather than dies, then run the fab with far fewer UPW rinse cycles and recycled rinse water, trading 1-3% capacity for yield-insensitive processing.
why: Water: ultrapure rinse volume is set by yield sensitivity to contamination; a defect-absorbing architecture lets the fab cut rinse volume ~10x, though metal contamination raising the leakage tail is the main risk.

title: Eliminate cell-level lithography: vapour-deposited, plasma-developed block copolymer holes
idea: Deposit a block copolymer film from vapour (iCVD) that self-assembles into a hexagonal hole array at the 4F2 pitch, guided by the transistor topography, and develop it by dry plasma removal of one block, with no spin coat, aqueous develop or wet strip.
why: Water and EUV: replaces the capacitor-hole EUV layer and its develop/strip water with a dry self-assembly step; ~10x less water for that layer and one fewer EUV pass.
